choice.stem: 다음 요약문의 빈칸 (A), (B), (C)에 들어갈 말로 가장 적절한 것을 고르시오.
choice.ex: (A) varied (B) structure (C) evolve 근거 ❹❺❻ 해설: (A) ❹ more variety → varied (diverse도 가능하지만 그 선지는 B·C가 틀림) / (B) ❺ the overall pattern of a book → structure (design도 가능하나 그 선지는 A·C 오류) / (C) ❻ development·unfolding → evolve (develop·unfold도 가능 — 그 선지들은 A·B 오류). 칸 하나만 보면 후보가 2~3개 → 두 칸 이상 교차해야 정답이 하나로 정해짐. 요약문 해석: 수업에서 발췌본을 읽으면 수업이 더 (A) 다양해지고 교사는 단조로움의 위험을 덜 수 있다. 그러나 조각만 접하는 학생들은 책의 완전한 (B) 구조를 보는 만족감을 놓치며, 작품이 진행되는 동안 (C) 발전해 가는 인물이나 주제 같은 특정한 문학적 특성은 짧은 발췌로 충분히 포착될 수 없다.
choice.psg: ❶ There is no doubt that the length of some literary works is overwhelming. ❷ Reading or translating a work in class, hour after hour, week after week, can be such a boring experience that many students never want to open a foreign language book again. ❸ Extracts provide one type of solution. ❹ The advantages are obvious: reading a series of passages from different works produces more variety in the classroom, so that the teacher has a greater chance of avoiding monotony, while still giving learners a taste at least of an author’s special flavour. ❺ On the other hand, a student who is only exposed to ‘bite-sized chunks’ will never have the satisfaction of knowing the overall pattern of a book, which is after all the satisfaction most of us seek when we read something in our own language. ❻ Moreover, there are some literary features that cannot be adequately illustrated by a short excerpt: the development of plot or character, for instance, with the gradual involvement of the reader that this implies; or the unfolding of a complex theme through the juxtaposition of contrasting views.
choice.body: Reading extracts in class can make lessons more (A)________ and spare teachers the risk of monotony. However, students who meet only fragments miss the satisfaction of seeing a book’s complete (B)________, and certain literary qualities, such as characters or themes that (C)________ over the course of a work, cannot be adequately captured in a short excerpt.

choice.stem: 다음 요약문의 빈칸 (A), (B), (C)에 들어갈 말로 가장 적절한 것을 고르시오.
choice.ex: (A) brief (B) deprived (C) native 근거 ❹❺ 해설: (A) ❹ a taste at least → brief (limited·quick도 성립, comprehensive·thorough는 at least와 모순) / (B) ❺ wil never have the satisfaction → deprived (robbed도 성립, assured·certain·proud는 반대) / (C) ❺ our own language → native (first도 성립, foreign·second는 글의 소재를 이 용한 함정). 요약문 해석: 발췌본은 학습자에게 최소한 다양한 작가의 문체를 (A) 짧게나마 맛보게 해 주지만, 발췌본을 넘어서지 않는 학생들은 책 한 권 전체를 따라 가는 데서 오는 만족감을 (B) 빼앗긴 채로 남는다. 그것은 바로 우리가 (C) 모국어로 읽을 때 찾는 만족감이다.
choice.psg: ❶ There is no doubt that the length of some literary works is overwhelming. ❷ Reading or translating a work in class, hour after hour, week after week, can be such a boring experience that many students never want to open a foreign language book again. ❸ Extracts provide one type of solution. ❹ The advantages are obvious: reading a series of passages from different works produces more variety in the classroom, so that the teacher has a greater chance of avoiding monotony, while still giving learners a taste at least of an author’s special flavour. ❺ On the other hand, a student who is only exposed to ‘bite-sized chunks’ will never have the satisfaction of knowing the overall pattern of a book, which is after all the satisfaction most of us seek when we read something in our own language. ❻ Moreover, there are some literary features that cannot be adequately illustrated by a short excerpt: the development of plot or character, for instance, with the gradual involvement of the reader that this implies; or the unfolding of a complex theme through the juxtaposition of contrasting views.
choice.body: Extracts give learners at least a (A)________ taste of various authors’ styles, but students who never go beyond them remain (B)________ of the fulfilment that comes from following a whole book — the very fulfilment we look for when reading in our (C)________ language.

choice.stem: 위 글에서 언급되지 않은 것을 고르시오.
opt: mandatory replacement of whole novels nationwide
limited representation of complex literary themes
broader range of authors in lessons
partial exposure to authors’ distinctive styles
choice.ex: 발췌본이 긴 작품의 대안이라는 이야기는 ❸❹에 있지만 ‘전국적·의무적’이라는 범위 한정어는 원문에 없음. 나머지는 ❷ / ❹ / ❹ / ❻에서 각각 확인. ① 근거 없음(정답) — 전국적인 장편 소설 의무 대체 ② 근거 ❻ — 복잡한 문학적 주제의 제한된 표현 ③ 근거 ❹ — 수업에서 더 폭넓은 작가의 범위 ④ 근거 ❷ — 외국어 서적에 대한 지속적인 거부감 ⑤ 근거 ❹ — 작가들의 독특한 문체에 대한 부분적 노출
choice.psg: ❶ There is no doubt that the length of some literary works is overwhelming. ❷ Reading or translating a work in class, hour after hour, week after week, can be such a boring experience that many students never want to open a foreign language book again. ❸ Extracts provide one type of solution. ❹ The advantages are obvious: reading a series of passages from different works produces more variety in the classroom, so that the teacher has a greater chance of avoiding monotony, while still giving learners a taste at least of an author’s special flavour. ❺ On the other hand, a student who is only exposed to ‘bite-sized chunks’ will never have the satisfaction of knowing the overall pattern of a book, which is after all the satisfaction most of us seek when we read something in our own language. ❻ Moreover, there are some literary features that cannot be adequately illustrated by a short excerpt: the development of plot or character, for instance, with the gradual involvement of the reader that this implies; or the unfolding of a complex theme through the juxtaposition of contrasting views.

choice.stem: 다음 글의 밑줄 친 부분이 의미하는 바로 가장 적절한 것을 고르시오.
opt: Extracts remove every drawback of reading whole works, so long novels are no longer needed in class.
Extracts ease the boredom of long works but offer only a partial solution to the problem.
Only teachers gain anything from extracts while students get nothing at all from them in class.
Extracts are chosen by teachers mainly to hide the weaknesses of long and difficult literary works.
Extracts work as a solution only when students have already finished reading the whole book.
choice.ex: 밑줄 해석: 발췌본은 (긴 작품을 수업에서 읽는 지루함에 대한) 한 가지 유형의 해결책을 제공한다. 해설: ‘one type of solution’ = ❷의 지루함에 대한 ‘여러 해결책 중 하나’ — 뒤 ❺❻(On the other hand, Moreover)이 한계를 제시하므로 부분적 해결. ① 발췌본은 작품 전체를 읽는 것의 모든 단점을 없애므로, 수업에서 긴 소설은 더 이상 필요 없다. 오답 — 범위 확대(every) ② 발췌본은 긴 작품의 지루함을 덜어 주지만 문제에 대한 부분적인 해결책만 제공한다. 정답 ③ 수업에서 학생들은 발췌본에서 아무것도 얻지 못하고 교사들만 무언가를 얻는다. 오답 — 범위 축소(교사만 이득) ④ 발췌본은 주로 길고 어려운 문학 작품의 약점을 숨기기 위해 교사들에 의해 선택된다. 오답 — 의도 심기(숨기려고) ⑤ 발췌본은 학생들이 이미 책 전체를 다 읽었을 때만 해결책으로 작동한다. 오답 — 조건·시점 왜곡(다 읽은 뒤에만)
choice.body: Reading or translating a work in class, hour after hour, week after week, can be such a boring experience that many students never want to open a foreign language book again. Extracts provide one type of solution. The advantages are obvious: reading a series of passages from different works produces more variety in the classroom, so that the teacher has a greater chance of avoiding monotony, while still giving learners a taste at least of an author’s special flavour.

choice.stem: 다음 요약문의 빈칸 (A), (B), (C)에 들어갈 말로 가장 적절한 것을 고르시오.
choice.ex: (A) reflects (B) inappropriate (C) adjust 근거 ❶❸❻❼❽ 해설: (A) ❶ reliable indicator → reflects (mirrors도 성립, conceals·disguises·exaggerates는 반대) / (B) ❸~❺ 규칙 위반·불편 → inappropriate (unsuitable도 성립, ideal·natural·comfortable이면 조절할 이유가 없음) / (C) ❻~❽ 눈맞춤을 줄이기도(엘리베이터) 늘리기도(큰 테이블) → adjust (modify·regulate도 성립, ignore·imitate는 오류). 두 칸 이상 교차해야 정답 하나로 좁혀짐. 요약문 해석: 사람들이 서로 사이에 얼마만큼의 공간을 두는지는 대체로 그들의 관계가 얼마나 가까운지를 (A) 반영한다. 그 물리적 거리가 (B) 부적절하 게 느껴질 때, 사람들은 편안한 심리적 거리를 회복하기 위해 눈맞춤 같은 다른 비언어적 신호를 (C) 조절한다.
choice.psg: ❶ Distance is a reliable indicator of the relationship between two people. ❷ Strangers stand further apart than do acquaintances, acquaintances stand further apart than friends, and friends stand further apart than romantic partners. ❸ Sometimes, of course, these rules are violated. ❹ Recall the last time you rode 20 stories in an elevator packed with total strangers. ❺ The sardine-like experience no doubt made the situation a bit uncomfortable. ❻ With your physical space violated, you may have tried to create “psychological” space by avoiding eye contact, focusing instead on the elevator buttons. ❼ By reducing closeness in one nonverbal channel (eye contact), one can compensate for unwanted closeness in another channel (proximity). ❽ Similarly, if you are talking with someone who is seated several feet away at a large table, you are likely to maintain constant eye contact — something you might feel uncomfortable doing if you were standing next to each other.
choice.body: How much space people leave between themselves generally (A)________ how close their relationship is; when that physical distance feels (B)________, people (C)________ other nonverbal signals, such as eye contact, to restore a comfortable psychological distance.

choice.stem: 다음 요약문의 빈칸 (A), (B), (C)에 들어갈 말로 가장 적절한 것을 고르시오.
choice.ex: (A) excessive (B) compensate (C) sustain 근거 ❹❻❼❽ 해설: (A) ❹❻ 꽉 찬 엘리베이터 → excessive (unwanted·unwelcome도 성립, insufficient·limited는 ❽의 반대 상황) / (B) ❼ compensate for (correct for도 성립, prepare·apologize·wait for는 뜻이 어긋남) / (C) ❽ maintain constant eye contact → sustain (maintain도 성립, avoid·reduce는 엘리베이터 상황을 거꾸로 끌어온 함정). 요약문 해석: 사람들이 (A) 과도한 물리적 가까움을 강요받을 때, 그들은 흔히 눈맞춤을 줄임으로써 그것을 (B) 보상한다. 반대로, 서로 멀리 떨어져 앉아 있을 때는 상호작용이 멀게 느껴지지 않도록 눈맞춤을 (C) 유지하는 경향이 있다.
choice.psg: ❶ Distance is a reliable indicator of the relationship between two people. ❷ Strangers stand further apart than do acquaintances, acquaintances stand further apart than friends, and friends stand further apart than romantic partners. ❸ Sometimes, of course, these rules are violated. ❹ Recall the last time you rode 20 stories in an elevator packed with total strangers. ❺ The sardine-like experience no doubt made the situation a bit uncomfortable. ❻ With your physical space violated, you may have tried to create “psychological” space by avoiding eye contact, focusing instead on the elevator buttons. ❼ By reducing closeness in one nonverbal channel (eye contact), one can compensate for unwanted closeness in another channel (proximity). ❽ Similarly, if you are talking with someone who is seated several feet away at a large table, you are likely to maintain constant eye contact — something you might feel uncomfortable doing if you were standing next to each other.
choice.body: When people are forced into (A)________ physical closeness, they often (B)________ for it by reducing eye contact; conversely, when they sit far from each other, they tend to (C)________ eye contact so that the interaction does not feel distant.

choice.stem: 위 글에서 언급되지 않은 것을 고르시오.
opt: cultural variation in preferred personal distance
consistent ranking of distance by relationship
increased eye contact across a large table

choice.psg: ❶ Distance is a reliable indicator of the relationship between two people. ❷ Strangers stand further apart than do acquaintances, acquaintances stand further apart than friends, and friends stand further apart than romantic partners. ❸ Sometimes, of course, these rules are violated. ❹ Recall the last time you rode 20 stories in an elevator packed with total strangers. ❺ The sardine-like experience no doubt made the situation a bit uncomfortable. ❻ With your physical space violated, you may have tried to create “psychological” space by avoiding eye contact, focusing instead on the elevator buttons. ❼ By reducing closeness in one nonverbal channel (eye contact), one can compensate for unwanted closeness in another channel (proximity). ❽ Similarly, if you are talking with someone who is seated several feet away at a large table, you are likely to maintain constant eye contact — something you might feel uncomfortable doing if you were standing next to each other.

choice.stem: 다음 글의 밑줄 친 부분이 의미하는 바로 가장 적절한 것을 고르시오.
opt: Passengers use their imagination to make the elevator seem much bigger than it really is.
Passengers reduce other signs of closeness to balance the physical closeness they cannot easily escape.
Passengers with poor social skills are the only ones who try to create distance in elevators.
Passengers avoid eye contact because they want to hide their identity from the strangers around them.
Passengers start friendly conversations so that the crowded elevator feels like a warm, shared space.
choice.ex: 밑줄 해석: 여러분은 눈을 마주치지 않고 엘리베이터 버튼에 집중함으로써 ‘심리적’ 공간을 만들어 내려고 했을 수도 있다. 해설: ‘심리적’ 공간 = 몸의 거리는 못 바꾸니 눈맞춤(다른 채널)을 줄여 마음의 거리를 확보 — 바로 뒤 ❼이 원리로 정리. ① 승객들은 상상력을 이용해 엘리베이터를 실제보다 훨씬 커 보이게 만든다. 오답 — ‘psychological’을 상상으로 오독 ② 승객들은 쉽게 벗어날 수 없는 물리적 가까움을 상쇄하기 위해 다른 가까움의 신호를 줄인다. 정답 ③ 사회성이 부족한 승객들만 엘리베이터에서 거리를 만들려고 한다. 오답 — 범위 축소(사회성 부족한 사람만) ④ 승객들은 주변의 낯선 사람들에게 자신의 정체를 숨기고 싶어서 눈맞춤을 피한다. 오답 — 의도 심기(정체 숨기기) ⑤ 승객들은 붐비는 엘리베이터가 따뜻한 공유 공간처럼 느껴지도록 친근한 대화를 시작한다. 오답 — 방향 뒤집기(가까움을 더함)
choice.body: The sardine-like experience no doubt made the situation a bit uncomfortable. With your physical space violated, you may have tried to create “psychological” space by avoiding eye contact, focusing instead on the elevator buttons. By reducing closeness in one nonverbal channel (eye contact), one can compensate for unwanted closeness in another channel (proximity).

choice.stem: 다음 요약문의 빈칸 (A), (B), (C)에 들어갈 말로 가장 적절한 것을 고르시오.
choice.ex: (A) fixed (B) interchangeable (C) expertise 근거 ❻❼❽❾ 해설: (A) ❽❾ 공식 지위와 무관 → 직급에 fixed되지 않음 (determined도 성립, rewarded·praised·shared는 오류) / (B) ❻ quite fluid → interchangeable (flexible·fluid도 성립, hierarchical·permanent는 반대) / (C) ❽❾ 음악·낚시의 판단력 → expertise (knowledge도 성립, seniority·age·salary는 ‘공식 지위’를 다시 끌어온 함정). 요약문 해석: 리더와 추종자의 역할은 공식 직급에 의해 영구적으로 (A) 고정되기보다는 (B) 서로 바뀔 수 있으며, 사람들의 목표와 당면한 일에 누구의 (C) 전문 지식이 가장 관련 있는지에 따라 바뀐다.
choice.psg: ❶ Followers can be defined by their position as subordinates or by their behavior of going along with leaders’ wishes. ❷ But followers also have power to lead. ❸ Followers empower leaders as well as vice versa. ❹ This has led some leadership analysts like Ronald Heifetz to avoid using the word followers and refer to the others in a power relationship as “citizens” or “constituents.” ❺ Heifetz is correct that too simple a view of followers can produce misunderstanding. ❻ In modern life, most people wind up being both leaders and followers, and the categories can become quite fluid. ❼ Our behavior as followers changes as our objectives change. ❽ If I trust your judgment in music more than my own, I may follow your lead on which concert we attend (even though you may be formally my subordinate in position). ❾ But if I am an expert on fishing, you may follow my lead on where we fish, regardless of our formal positions or the fact that I followed your lead on concerts yesterday.
choice.body: Rather than being permanently (A)________ by official rank, the roles of leader and follower are (B)________, shifting with people’s goals and with whose (C)________ is most relevant to the task at hand.

choice.stem: 다음 요약문의 빈칸 (A), (B), (C)에 들어갈 말로 가장 적절한 것을 고르시오.
choice.ex: (A) empower (B) simplistic (C) lead 근거 ❷❸❹❺❽❾ 해설: (A) ❷❸ also ~ empower (strengthen도 성립, obey·fear·imitate는 ‘also’의 반전 의미가 없음) / (B) ❺ too simple → simplistic (narrow도 성 립, nuanced·balanced·complex는 반대) / (C) ❽❾ defer ↔ yet 대조 → lead (direct·guide도 성립, comply·hesitate는 defer와 같은 쪽). 요약문 해석: 추종자도 자신을 이끄는 사람들에게 (A) 힘을 실어 주기 때문에, 일부 분석가들은 ‘추종자’라는 꼬리표를 피하며 추종에 대한 지나치게 (B) 단 순한 개념이 오해를 낳는다고 경고한다. 실제로 같은 사람이 어떤 문제에서는 남에게 따르면서 다른 문제에서는 (C) 이끌 수 있다.
choice.psg: ❶ Followers can be defined by their position as subordinates or by their behavior of going along with leaders’ wishes. ❷ But followers also have power to lead. ❸ Followers empower leaders as well as vice versa. ❹ This has led some leadership analysts like Ronald Heifetz to avoid using the word followers and refer to the others in a power relationship as “citizens” or “constituents.” ❺ Heifetz is correct that too simple a view of followers can produce misunderstanding. ❻ In modern life, most people wind up being both leaders and followers, and the categories can become quite fluid. ❼ Our behavior as followers changes as our objectives change. ❽ If I trust your judgment in music more than my own, I may follow your lead on which concert we attend (even though you may be formally my subordinate in position). ❾ But if I am an expert on fishing, you may follow my lead on where we fish, regardless of our formal positions or the fact that I followed your lead on concerts yesterday.
choice.body: Because followers also (A)________ those who guide them, some analysts avoid the label “followers,” warning that an overly (B)________ notion of followership breeds misunderstanding; indeed, the same person may defer to another on one matter yet (C)________ on another.

choice.stem: 위 글에서 언급되지 않은 것을 고르시오.
opt: alternative labels for people under authority
risks of an oversimplified view of followers
reciprocal influence between leaders and followers
greater trust in another’s musical judgment
official adoption of Heifetz’s terms by companies
choice.ex: Heifetz의 용어 변경은 ❹에 있지만 ‘기업들의 공식 채택’이라는 범위 한정어는 원문에 없음. 나머지는 ❸ / ❹ / ❺ / ❽에서 각각 확 인. ① 근거 ❹ — 권한 아래 있는 사람들에 대한 대안적 명칭 ② 근거 ❺ — 추종자에 대한 지나치게 단순화된 관점의 위험 ③ 근거 ❸ — 리더와 추종자 사이의 상호 영향 ④ 근거 ❽ — 다른 사람의 음악적 판단에 대한 더 큰 신뢰 ⑤ 근거 없음(정답) — 기업들의 Heifetz 용어 공식 채택
choice.psg: ❶ Followers can be defined by their position as subordinates or by their behavior of going along with leaders’ wishes. ❷ But followers also have power to lead. ❸ Followers empower leaders as well as vice versa. ❹ This has led some leadership analysts like Ronald Heifetz to avoid using the word followers and refer to the others in a power relationship as “citizens” or “constituents.” ❺ Heifetz is correct that too simple a view of followers can produce misunderstanding. ❻ In modern life, most people wind up being both leaders and followers, and the categories can become quite fluid. ❼ Our behavior as followers changes as our objectives change. ❽ If I trust your judgment in music more than my own, I may follow your lead on which concert we attend (even though you may be formally my subordinate in position). ❾ But if I am an expert on fishing, you may follow my lead on where we fish, regardless of our formal positions or the fact that I followed your lead on concerts yesterday.

choice.stem: 다음 글의 밑줄 친 부분이 의미하는 바로 가장 적절한 것을 고르시오.
opt: People pretend to follow others in order to hide their real intention of controlling them.
People can switch between guiding others and following them according to the particular situation they face.
People who become leaders are steadily increasing in number in most modern societies around the world today.
People usually move in only one direction as they grow older, from followers to guides.
People in different cultures use different labels like citizens for the very same group of followers.
choice.ex: 밑줄 해석: 현대의 삶에서 대부분의 사람들은 결국 리더와 추종자가 둘 다 되고, 그 범주는 꽤 유동적일 수 있다. 해설: ‘fluid’ = 리더/추종자 범주가 고정되지 않고 상황에 따라 오감 — 바로 뒤 ❼ ‘목표가 변하면 추종 행동도 변한다’. ① 사람들은 남을 통제하려는 진짜 의도를 숨기기 위해 따르는 척한다. 오답 — 의도 심기 ② 사람들은 자신이 처한 특정 상황에 따라 남을 이끄는 것과 따르는 것 사이를 오갈 수 있다. 정답 ③ 오늘날 대부분의 현대 사회에서 리더가 되는 사람들의 수가 꾸준히 늘고 있다. 오답 — 수치 비틀기(수 증가) ④ 사람들은 보통 나이가 들면서 추종자에서 안내자로, 한 방향으로만 움직인다. 오답 — 시점 이동(나이에 따른 한 방향 변화) ⑤ 서로 다른 문화의 사람들은 똑같은 추종자 집단에 대해 ‘시민’ 같은 서로 다른 꼬리표를 쓴다. 오답 — 주체 바꿔치기([4]의 용어 문제로 이동)
choice.body: Heifetz is correct that too simple a view of followers can produce misunderstanding. In modern life, most people wind up being both leaders and followers, and the categories can become quite fluid. Our behavior as followers changes as our objectives change.
choice.ul: the categories can become quite fluid.

choice.stem: 다음 요약문의 빈칸 (A), (B), (C)에 들어갈 말로 가장 적절한 것을 고르시오.
choice.ex: (A) shun (B) unpleasant (C) fades 근거 ❶❷❼❽❾ 해설: (A) ❶❷ → shun (avoid·reject도 성립, crave·seek는 반대) / (B) ❽ bad and even disgusting → unpleasant (nasty도 성립, bland는 ‘밍밍 한’이라 disgusting과 다르고 sweet·delicious는 반대) / (C) ❾ no longer taste as bad → fades (weakens도 성립, returns·spreads·intensifies는 오류). 요약문 해석: 동물과 어린아이 모두 항영양소가 풍부한 식물을 (A) 피하는 타고난 경향이 있다. 아이들의 경우, 아직 취약할 때 몸이 그런 음식을 (B) 불쾌 한 맛이 나게 만들지만, 이 거부감은 그것을 감당할 만큼 강하게 자라면 (C) 사라진다.
choice.psg: ❶ In the natural world, if an animal consumes a plant with enough antinutrients to make it feel unwell, it won’t eat that plant again. ❷ Intuitively, animals also know to stay away from these plants. ❸ Years of evolution and information being passed down created this innate intelligence. ❹ This “intuition,” though, is not just seen in animals. ❺ Have you ever wondered why most children hate vegetables? ❻ Dr. Steven Gundry justifies this as part of our genetic programming, our inner intelligence. ❼ Since many vegetables are full of antinutrients, your body tries to keep you away from them while you are still fragile and in development. ❽ It does this by making your taste buds perceive these flavors as bad and even disgusting. ❾ As you grow and your body becomes stronger enough to tolerate these antinutrients, suddenly they no longer taste as bad as before.
choice.body: Both animals and young children have an inborn tendency to (A)________ plants rich in antinutrients; in children, the body makes such foods taste (B)________ while they are still vulnerable, but this aversion (C)________ once they have grown strong enough to handle them.

choice.stem: 다음 요약문의 빈칸 (A), (B), (C)에 들어갈 말로 가장 적절한 것을 고르시오.
choice.ex: (A) inherited (B) repulsive (C) withstand 근거 ❻❼❽❾ 해설: (A) ❻ genetic programming → inherited (inborn도 성립, acquired·learned·social은 ‘경험으로 배운다’는 반대 함정) / (B) ❽ disgusting → repulsive (revolting·unappetizing도 성립, nutritious·tasty는 반대) / (C) ❾ tolerate → withstand (tolerate는 원문 단어로 성립, identify·produce·remove는 오류). 요약문 해석: Gundry 박사에 따르면, 아이들의 채소 거부는 단순한 까다로움이 아니라 (A) 물려받은 형태의 보호이다. 그들의 몸은 음식에 들어 있는 항영 양소를 (C) 견딜 수 있을 때까지 이 음식들을 (B) 혐오스럽게 보이도록 만든다.
choice.psg: ❶ In the natural world, if an animal consumes a plant with enough antinutrients to make it feel unwell, it won’t eat that plant again. ❷ Intuitively, animals also know to stay away from these plants. ❸ Years of evolution and information being passed down created this innate intelligence. ❹ This “intuition,” though, is not just seen in animals. ❺ Have you ever wondered why most children hate vegetables? ❻ Dr. Steven Gundry justifies this as part of our genetic programming, our inner intelligence. ❼ Since many vegetables are full of antinutrients, your body tries to keep you away from them while you are still fragile and in development. ❽ It does this by making your taste buds perceive these flavors as bad and even disgusting. ❾ As you grow and your body becomes stronger enough to tolerate these antinutrients, suddenly they no longer taste as bad as before.
choice.body: According to Dr. Gundry, children’s rejection of vegetables is not mere fussiness but an (A)________ form of protection: their bodies make these foods seem (B)________ until they can (C)________ the antinutrients the foods contain.

choice.stem: 위 글에서 언급되지 않은 것을 고르시오.
opt: milder taste of vegetables after physical growth
inborn intelligence shaped by long adaptation
widespread dislike of vegetables among children
lasting avoidance of harmful plants by animals
exact age of greater tolerance for vegetables
choice.ex: 성장 후 맛의 변화는 ❾에 있지만 ‘정확한 나이’라는 수치 한정어는 원문에 없음. 나머지는 ❶❷ / ❸ / ❺ / ❾에서 각각 확인. ① 근거 ❾ — 신체 성장 이후 더 순해진 채소 맛 ② 근거 ❸ — 오랜 적응으로 형성된 타고난 지능 ③ 근거 ❺ — 아이들 사이에 널리 퍼진 채소 거부 ④ 근거 ❶❷ — 동물의 해로운 식물에 대한 지속적 회피 ⑤ 근거 없음(정답) — 채소를 더 잘 견디게 되는 정확한 나이
choice.psg: ❶ In the natural world, if an animal consumes a plant with enough antinutrients to make it feel unwell, it won’t eat that plant again. ❷ Intuitively, animals also know to stay away from these plants. ❸ Years of evolution and information being passed down created this innate intelligence. ❹ This “intuition,” though, is not just seen in animals. ❺ Have you ever wondered why most children hate vegetables? ❻ Dr. Steven Gundry justifies this as part of our genetic programming, our inner intelligence. ❼ Since many vegetables are full of antinutrients, your body tries to keep you away from them while you are still fragile and in development. ❽ It does this by making your taste buds perceive these flavors as bad and even disgusting. ❾ As you grow and your body becomes stronger enough to tolerate these antinutrients, suddenly they no longer taste as bad as before.

choice.stem: 다음 글의 밑줄 친 부분이 의미하는 바로 가장 적절한 것을 고르시오.
opt: Children decide to dislike vegetables in order to get more attention from their busy parents.
Children’s bodies reject vegetables only after they have become strong enough to digest them fully.
Children’s bodies damage their own taste buds so that no flavors can be sensed at all.
Children’s bodies use bad flavors as a warning to protect them from harmful food while growing.
Children’s bodies make vegetables taste sweet so that they will eat more while still growing.
choice.ex: 밑줄 해석: 그것(몸)은 여러분의 미뢰로 하여금 이러한 맛을 나쁘고 심지어 역겨운 것으로 인식하게 만듦으로써 이를 수행한다. 해설: ‘It does this’의 this = ❼ 몸이 연약한 아이를 항영양소에서 멀리하게 하는 일 → 역겨운 맛 = 경고 신호. ① 아이들은 바쁜 부모에게서 더 많은 관심을 받으려고 채소를 싫어하기로 결심한다. 오답 — 의도 심기(관심 끌기) ② 아이들의 몸은 채소를 완전히 소화할 만큼 강해진 뒤에야 채소를 거부한다. 오답 — 시점 이동(강해진 뒤에) ③ 아이들의 몸은 자신의 미뢰를 손상시켜 어떤 맛도 전혀 느낄 수 없게 한다. 오답 — 정도 과장(맛을 전혀 못 느낌) ④ 아이들의 몸은 나쁜 맛을 경고로 사용해 성장하는 동안 그들을 해로운 음식으로부터 보호한다. 정답 ⑤ 아이들의 몸은 아직 자라는 동안 채소를 더 많이 먹도록 채소를 단맛이 나게 만든다. 오답 — 방향 뒤집기(단맛)
choice.body: Since many vegetables are full of antinutrients, your body tries to keep you away from them while you are still fragile and in development. It does this by making your taste buds perceive these flavors as bad and even disgusting. As you grow and your body becomes stronger enough to tolerate these antinutrients, suddenly they no longer taste as bad as before.
choice.ul: making your taste buds perceive these flavors as bad and even disgusting.

choice.stem: 다음 요약문의 빈칸 (A), (B), (C)에 들어갈 말로 가장 적절한 것을 고르시오.
choice.ex: (A) diminished (B) unfounded (C) override 근거 ❶❻❽❾ 해설: (A) ❻ 8% less → diminished (reduced도 성립, increased·doubled·fixed는 오류) / (B) ❶❽ blind, blindly → unfounded (baseless도 성 립, verified·scientific·careful은 ‘이름만 보고 추측’과 모순) / (C) ❾ 선입견이 자기 소득을 깎게 함 → override (outweigh·overpower도 성립, support·improve는 선입견과 합리성을 같은 방향으로 본 오독). 요약문 해석: 덴마크 십 대들은 이름이 공통된 배경을 암시하는 사람과 일하는 대가로 (A) 줄어든 급여를 기꺼이 받아들였는데, 이는 (B) 근거 없는 가정에 뿌리를 둔 선입견이 합리적인 금전적 판단을 (C) 압도할 수 있음을 보여 준다.
choice.psg: ❶ A study investigated the economic cost of prejudice based on blind assumptions. ❷ Researchers gave a group of Danish teenagers the choice of working with one of two people. ❸ The teenager had never met either of them. ❹ One of the people had a name that suggested they were from a similar ethnic or religious background to the teenager. ❺ The other had a name that suggested they were from a different ethnic or religious background. ❻ The study showed that the teenagers were prepared to earn an average of 8% less if they could work with someone they thought came from the same ethnic or religious background. ❼ And this prejudice was evident among teenagers with ethnic majority names as well as those with ethnic minority names. ❽ The teenagers were blindly making assumptions about the race of their potential colleagues. ❾ They then applied prejudice to those assumptions, to the point where they actually allowed that prejudice to reduce their own potential income. ❿ The job required the two teenagers to work together for just 90 minutes.
choice.body: Danish teenagers were willing to accept (A)________ pay in exchange for working with someone whose name implied a shared background, revealing that a prejudice rooted in (B)________ assumptions can (C)________ rational financial judgment.

choice.stem: 다음 요약문의 빈칸 (A), (B), (C)에 들어갈 말로 가장 적절한 것을 고르시오.
choice.ex: (A) striking (B) brief (C) earnings 근거 ❼❾❿ 해설: (A) 단 90분 협업을 위해 소득 포기 → 더욱 놀라운 일 = striking (surprising·remarkable도 성립, understandable·reasonable은 ‘짧으니 괜찮 다’는 반대 논리) / (B) ❿ just 90 minutes → brief (short도 성립, considerable·lengthy·long은 반대) / (C) ❾ their own potential income → earnings (income도 성립, reputation·friendships·health는 원문에 없는 대상). 요약문 해석: 그 편견은 다수·소수 집단 십 대 모두에게서 나타났고, 협업이 (B) 짧은 시간 동안만 지속될 것임을 고려하면 더욱 (A) 놀라운데, 이는 사람들 이 자신과 다르다고 여기는 사람과 일하는 것을 피하기 위해 자신의 (C) 소득을 희생할 수 있음을 시사한다.
choice.psg: ❶ A study investigated the economic cost of prejudice based on blind assumptions. ❷ Researchers gave a group of Danish teenagers the choice of working with one of two people. ❸ The teenager had never met either of them. ❹ One of the people had a name that suggested they were from a similar ethnic or religious background to the teenager. ❺ The other had a name that suggested they were from a different ethnic or religious background. ❻ The study showed that the teenagers were prepared to earn an average of 8% less if they could work with someone they thought came from the same ethnic or religious background. ❼ And this prejudice was evident among teenagers with ethnic majority names as well as those with ethnic minority names. ❽ The teenagers were blindly making assumptions about the race of their potential colleagues. ❾ They then applied prejudice to those assumptions, to the point where they actually allowed that prejudice to reduce their own potential income. ❿ The job required the two teenagers to work together for just 90 minutes.
choice.body: The bias appeared among both majority and minority teenagers, and it was all the more (A)________ given that the collaboration would last only a (B)________ time, suggesting that people may sacrifice their own (C)________ to avoid working with those they see as different.

opt: The teenagers asked their possible coworkers directly in interviews about their ethnic and religious backgrounds.
The teenagers formed their judgment of race only after working with their new partners for months.
The teenagers judged the background of complete strangers from nothing more than their written names.

para.en: There is no doubt that the length of some literary works is overwhelming. Reading or translating a work in class, hour after hour, week after week, can be such a boring experience that many students never want to open a foreign language book again. Extracts provide one type of solution. The advantages are obvious: reading a series of passages from different works produces more variety in the classroom, so that the teacher has a greater chance of avoiding monotony, while still giving learners a taste at least of an author’s special flavour. On the other hand, a student who is only exposed to ‘bite-sized chunks’ will never have the satisfaction of knowing the overall pattern of a book, which is after all the satisfaction most of us seek when we read something in our own language. Moreover, there are some literary features that cannot be adequately illustrated by a short excerpt: the development of plot or character, for instance, with the gradual involvement of the reader that this implies; or the unfolding of a complex theme through the juxtaposition of contrasting views.

Distance is a reliable indicator of the relationship between two people. Strangers stand further apart than do acquaintances, acquaintances stand further apart than friends, and friends stand further apart than romantic partners. Sometimes, of course, these rules are violated. Recall the last time you rode 20 stories in an elevator packed with total strangers. The sardine-like experience no doubt made the situation a bit uncomfortable. With your physical space violated, you may have tried to create “psychological” space by avoiding eye contact, focusing instead on the elevator buttons. By reducing closeness in one nonverbal channel (eye contact), one can compensate for unwanted closeness in another channel (proximity). Similarly, if you are talking with someone who is seated several feet away at a large table, you are likely to maintain constant eye contact — something you might feel uncomfortable doing if you were standing next to each other.

Followers can be defined by their position as subordinates or by their behavior of going along with leaders’ wishes. But followers also have power to lead. Followers empower leaders as well as vice versa. This has led some leadership analysts like Ronald Heifetz to avoid using the word followers and refer to the others in a power relationship as “citizens” or “constituents.” Heifetz is correct that too simple a view of followers can produce misunderstanding. In modern life, most people wind up being both leaders and followers, and the categories can become quite fluid. Our behavior as followers changes as our objectives change. If I trust your judgment in music more than my own, I may follow your lead on which concert we attend (even though you may be formally my subordinate in position). But if I am an expert on fishing, you may follow my lead on where we fish, regardless of our formal positions or the fact that I followed your lead on concerts yesterday.

In the natural world, if an animal consumes a plant with enough antinutrients to make it feel unwell, it won’t eat that plant again. Intuitively, animals also know to stay away from these plants. Years of evolution and information being passed down created this innate intelligence. This “intuition,” though, is not just seen in animals. Have you ever wondered why most children hate vegetables? Dr. Steven Gundry justifies this as part of our genetic programming, our inner intelligence. Since many vegetables are full of antinutrients, your body tries to keep you away from them while you are still fragile and in development. It does this by making your taste buds perceive these flavors as bad and even disgusting. As you grow and your body becomes stronger enough to tolerate these antinutrients, suddenly they no longer taste as bad as before.

A study investigated the economic cost of prejudice based on blind assumptions. Researchers gave a group of Danish teenagers the choice of working with one of two people. The teenager had never met either of them. One of the people had a name that suggested they were from a similar ethnic or religious background to the teenager. The other had a name that suggested they were from a different ethnic or religious background. The study showed that the teenagers were prepared to earn an average of 8% less if they could work with someone they thought came from the same ethnic or religious background. And this prejudice was evident among teenagers with ethnic majority names as well as those with ethnic minority names. The teenagers were blindly making assumptions about the race of their potential colleagues. They then applied prejudice to those assumptions, to the point where they actually allowed that prejudice to reduce their own potential income. The job required the two teenagers to work together for just 90 minutes.
